content:
Hi everyone!
I just read the #Nova > Getting started with nova contribution and #Nova > Good first issue and I realize that it might be hard for me to contribute the Nova now.

I'm still pretty new to Rust and Linux kernel development, so I'll probably start with Rust for Linux to build up some experience first.

I'd still like to follow Nova's development and get to know the community in the meantime.

Would reading the mailing list and following patch discussions be a good place to start? Is there anything else you'd recommend?

Thanks!

Would reading the mailing list and following patch discussions be a good place to start?

Yeah, that is what I usually recommend -- read a few threads in Lore to see how the mailing list works and the dynamic there, then read/review/test a couple patches that you feel comfortable about (you can reply to old messages you don't have in your inbox -- Lore give the instructions are the bottom of the page if you click on "permalink"), and consider giving your Reviewed-by and/or Tested-by tags! :)

(You may want to move this thread to #Help later on)

Thanks Miguel! I'll start reading some Nova patch discussions on Lore.

If I come across something I don't understand, would it be okay to ask about it here in the Nova channel, or would the Help channel be a better place for those questions?
